title: 10 000$ Home Gym Tour - 10k subs special
summary: For the 10k-subscriber special, NH tours the garage gym he built himself: a custom 16x9 ft three-layer platform, Rogue rack and bars, an SSB, dumbbells, calibrated plates and assorted accessories. It's worth about $12,000 but cost him around $7,000 thanks to DIY and smart buying. He shares the money-saving tips and his daily training habits.
claims: His garage gym took 3-4 months to plan, clean and build
The gym is worth about $12,000 but cost him about $7,000 by cutting corners smartly
Don't lift on concrete; dropped weights shatter it, and it's bad for stability and knees
His custom 16x9 ft platform cost $800-900 versus an estimated $5,000-6,000 if contracted
Garage floors slope toward the door for drainage, so a platform must be shimmed level or the barbell rolls
Platform layers: plastic vapor barrier (arctic climate), mid-quality plywood, glued stall mats, high-quality plywood on top
Buy plywood in person, since ordered plywood is often warped
Buy equipment directly from manufacturers' sales reps and bundle purchases for discounts and free shipping
The Rogue fat pad bench is great for wide or problematic shoulders
Box squats are inferior; he uses his box for box front squats and SSB box squats for deadlift carryover
His favorite bar is a Rogue Ohio Power Bar (~$400), with a second one as a beater bar for rack pulls bought from the Boneyard for ~$180
EliteFTS refunded the difference when the SSB went on sale the day after he paid full price
A quality EZ curl bar ($150-200) is worth it for curl bros
He does dumbbell pullovers every day or two at 5-12 reps with 60 lb to build lats and expand the rib cage
A rack is the most important home gym item if you want to train legs
He trains grip with grippers (1, 1.5, 2) every two days
Train finger extension with rubber bands; it feels good on the elbows and develops the forearms
He uses a Slingshot to protect a right shoulder he wrecked benching
DIY roller J-cups cost about $30 and save your knurling
Use $1 spring clamps from a hardware store instead of collars during warm-ups
Get spotter arms if you train alone; don't die under the bar
Chalk marks on the rack let him repeat exact pin heights for partials, pin press, squats and front squats
He needs a lift-off (portable monolith) to bench, or his shoulder positioning gets destroyed
He spent about $2,000-3,000 on plates, all calibrated, and needed extra 10s and 5s for dumbbell work
A $40 hardware-store mirror does the job versus $1,000 quotes; he uses it to check squat form
LeBron lifestyle sneakers are his favorite lifting shoes
He trains 2-3 hours every day except Sunday
The channel's core value is a community where natural lifters gather and learn; numbers don't matter
exercises: 60 lb, 5-12 reps, daily or every other day
